title: The J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 – Section-wise Mapping

blocks.title: The J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019
blocks.subtitle: The Legal Framework for the Reorganisation of Jammu & Kashmir

blocks.title: Overview of the Act
blocks.content: The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 was enacted by the Parliament of India on 9th August 2019. It received the President's assent on 9th August 2019 and came into force on 31st October 2019. The Act provides for the reorganisation of the state of Jammu & Kashmir into two Union Territories: Jammu & Kashmir (with legislature) and Ladakh (without legislature).

blocks.title: Structure of the Act
blocks.content: The Act consists of: **103 Sections** divided into **14 Parts**; and **5 Schedules**. It comprehensively covers the establishment of the two UTs, the composition of legislatures, the application of central laws, and the transitional provisions.

blocks.title: The 14 Parts of the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019
rows: Reorganisation of the State of Jammu & Kashmir
Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir (Legislative Assembly)
High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh

blocks.title: The 5 Schedules of the Act
rows: Amendments to the Constitution (Application of provisions)
Representation of Union Territories in the Rajya Sabha
Allocation of 4 seats in Rajya Sabha to the UT of J&K
Application of Central Laws and Repeal of State Laws (106 Central Laws applied; 153 State Laws repealed)

blocks.title: Example: Key Provisions Summary
given: The Act reorganised J&K into two Union Territories.
blocks.find: What are the key structural changes?
steps: The state of J&K was bifurcated into UT of J&K (with legislature) and UT of Ladakh (without legislature).
The UT of J&K has a Legislative Assembly with 83-90 seats (after delimitation).
The UT of Ladakh is governed directly by the President, through an Administrator.
The Act applies 106 Central Laws and repeals 153 State Laws.
The High Court of J&K and Ladakh was established (common High Court).
The Act provides for the allocation of 4 Rajya Sabha seats to J&K.
blocks.answer: The Act created two UTs, defined legislative and executive structures, and streamlined laws.

blocks.title: Trap: The Act came into force on 9th August 2019.
blocks.wrong: The Act came into force on 9th August 2019.
blocks.correct: The Act received assent on 9th August 2019 but came into force on 31st October 2019.
blocks.tip: Assent date vs. enforcement date: 9th August 2019 (assent); 31st October 2019 (commencement).

blocks.title: Key Points – Structural Blueprint
points: Two UTs: J&K (with legislature) and Ladakh (without legislature).
5 Schedules: First (Constitution amendments), Second (Assets/Liabilities), Third (Rajya Sabha representation), Fourth (4 seats for J&K), Fifth (106 Central laws, 153 State laws repealed).

subtopics.title: Part II – Reorganisation: Section 3 and Section 4

blocks.title: Part II – Reorganisation
blocks.subtitle: Section 3 and Section 4 – The Core of the Act

blocks.title: Section 3 – Formation of Union Territory of Ladakh
blocks.content: Section 3 of the Act provides for the formation of the Union Territory of Ladakh. It states that the existing state of Jammu & Kashmir shall be reorganised into two Union Territories. The UT of Ladakh shall comprise the districts of Kargil and Leh. It shall not have a Legislative Assembly. The President shall administer Ladakh through an Administrator (Lieutenant Governor).

blocks.title: Section 4 – Formation of Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir
blocks.content: Section 4 provides for the formation of the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir. It shall comprise the remaining territory of the erstwhile state (excluding Ladakh). It shall have a Legislative Assembly. The President shall administer J&K through a Lieutenant Governor, with a Council of Ministers headed by a Chief Minister.

blocks.title: Section 3 vs Section 4 – Comparison
rows: Legislative Assembly can make laws on State List subjects (except Police, Public Order)

blocks.title: Example: Understanding Section 3 and 4
given: Section 3 and 4 are the core reorganisation provisions.
blocks.find: What is the significance of these sections?
steps: Section 3 creates Ladakh as a UT without a legislature.
Section 4 creates J&K as a UT with a legislature.
This bifurcation is the fundamental restructuring of the erstwhile state.
Ladakh's administration is directly under the President.
J&K's administration has a democratic structure with CM and Council.
blocks.answer: Sections 3 and 4 define the two UTs and their respective governance structures.

blocks.title: Trap: J&K has no legislature.
blocks.wrong: UT of J&K has no Legislative Assembly.
blocks.correct: UT of J&K has a Legislative Assembly (with elections).
blocks.tip: J&K UT has a legislature; Ladakh UT does not.

blocks.title: Key Points – Part II
points: Section 3: UT of Ladakh (Leh, Kargil) – no legislature.
J&K: LG + CM + Council of Ministers.

subtopics.title: Part III – Legislative Assembly Structure: Article 239A, LG's Powers, Section 15, Section 32

blocks.title: Part III – Legislative Assembly Structure
blocks.subtitle: Composition, Powers, and the Role of the Lieutenant Governor

blocks.title: Application of Article 239A to J&K
blocks.content: Article 239A provides for the creation of a legislature for certain Union Territories. The J&K Reorganisation Act applies Article 239A to the UT of Jammu & Kashmir, following the Puducherry model. This allows for a Legislative Assembly with elected members, a Chief Minister, and a Council of Ministers. The Lieutenant Governor is the head, but the executive power is exercised by the Council of Ministers on the aid and advice of the LG.

blocks.title: Powers of the Lieutenant Governor (LG)
blocks.content:
The LG of J&K has significant powers under the Act:
1. **Nomination of Women Members** (Section 15): The LG can nominate two women members to the Legislative Assembly if they are not adequately represented.
2. **Nomination of Kashmiri Migrants/Displaced Persons**: Recent amendments allow the LG to nominate two members from the Kashmiri migrant community and one from the displaced persons of PoK.
3. **Discretionary Powers**: The LG can act in his discretion in matters where the Constitution or the Act confers such power (e.g., reservation of bills for President's consideration, promulgation of ordinances when the Assembly is not in session).

blocks.title: Section 15 – Nomination of Women Members
blocks.content: Section 15 of the Act empowers the LG to nominate up to two women members to the Legislative Assembly if, in his opinion, women are not adequately represented. This is a special provision to ensure gender representation.

blocks.title: Section 32 – Scope of Legislative Powers
blocks.content: Section 32 defines the legislative competence of the J&K Legislative Assembly. It restricts the Assembly's power on two subjects: **Police** and **Public Order** (Entries 1 and 2 of the State List). These subjects are under the control of the Lieutenant Governor and the Central Government. The Assembly can make laws on other State List subjects.

blocks.title: Key Provisions of Part III
rows: Two Kashmiri migrants + one displaced person of PoK
Assembly cannot make laws on Police and Public Order
Aid and advice to LG (like Puducherry)

blocks.title: Example: Section 32 in Action
given: Section 32 restricts legislative powers on Police and Public Order.
blocks.find: Why are these subjects excluded from the Assembly's purview?
steps: Police and Public Order are sensitive subjects related to internal security.
The Union Territory is under the administrative control of the MHA.
The LG has direct authority over these matters.
This ensures that the Central Government retains control over law and order.
The provision reflects the special status of J&K as a UT.
blocks.answer: Police and Public Order are excluded to ensure central control over internal security.

blocks.title: Trap: The LG has no discretionary powers.
blocks.wrong: The LG always acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.
blocks.correct: The LG has discretionary powers in certain matters (e.g., reservation of bills, ordinances).
blocks.tip: LG has discretion in matters where the Act confers such power.

blocks.title: Key Points – Part III
points: LG nominates Kashmiri migrants and displaced persons (recent amendments).
Section 32: Assembly cannot legislate on Police and Public Order.
Council of Ministers aids and advises LG.

subtopics.title: Practice MCQs: Structural Blueprint & Part II/III

blocks.title: Exam Strategy
blocks.content: Focus on the exact section numbers, the number of parts and schedules, the distinction between the two UTs, the application of Article 239A, and the restrictions under Section 32. Memorize key dates and provisions.

blocks.question: The J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 came into force on which date?
blocks.explanation: The Act received assent on 9th August 2019 but came into force on 31st October 2019.

blocks.question: How many sections does the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 contain?
blocks.explanation: The Act has 103 Sections, 14 Parts, and 5 Schedules.

blocks.question: Which Section of the Act provides for the formation of the UT of Ladakh?
blocks.explanation: Section 3 provides for the formation of the UT of Ladakh.

blocks.question: Which UT has a Legislative Assembly as per the Act?
blocks.explanation: UT of J&K has a Legislative Assembly; Ladakh does not.

blocks.question: How many Rajya Sabha seats are allocated to the UT of J&K under the Fourth Schedule?
blocks.explanation: The Fourth Schedule allocates 4 Rajya Sabha seats to J&K.

blocks.question: Which Article of the Constitution is applied to the UT of J&K for its legislative structure?
blocks.explanation: Article 239A (Puducherry model) is applied to J&K.

blocks.question: Section 32 of the Act restricts legislative powers on which subjects?
blocks.explanation: Section 32 restricts the Assembly from legislating on Police and Public Order.

blocks.question: The LG can nominate how many women members to the Legislative Assembly under Section 15?
blocks.explanation: Section 15 allows the LG to nominate two women members if inadequately represented.

blocks.question: Which Schedule of the Act deals with the application of Central Laws and repeal of State Laws?
blocks.explanation: The Fifth Schedule provides for the application of 106 Central Laws and repeal of 153 State Laws.

blocks.question: Who administers the UT of Ladakh?
blocks.explanation: Ladakh is administered by a Lieutenant Governor (Administrator) appointed by the President.

blocks.title: Post-Test Review
blocks.content: Review the structure (103 Sections, 14 Parts, 5 Schedules), the distinction between UTs, the LG's powers, and Section 32 restrictions. Memorize key section numbers.
points: Section 32: No powers on Police and Public Order.
Fifth Schedule: 106 Central Laws applied, 153 State Laws repealed.

subtopics.title: Fourth Schedule – Allocation of Rajya Sabha Seats to J&K

blocks.title: Fourth Schedule – Rajya Sabha Representation
blocks.subtitle: Allocation of 4 Seats to the UT of J&K

blocks.title: What is the Fourth Schedule?
blocks.content: The Fourth Schedule of the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 deals with the representation of the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir in the Rajya Sabha (Council of States). It allocates 4 seats to the UT of J&K in the Rajya Sabha.

blocks.title: Key Provisions of the Fourth Schedule
blocks.content:
1. **Allocation of Seats**: The UT of J&K is allocated 4 seats in the Rajya Sabha.
2. **Manner of Election**: Members are elected by the Legislative Assembly of J&K through proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote.
3. **Term**: The term of Rajya Sabha members is 6 years, with one-third retiring every two years.
4. **Comparison with Erstwhile State**: The erstwhile state of J&K had 6 Rajya Sabha seats; the UT has been reduced to 4 seats.

blocks.title: Rajya Sabha Seats – Pre and Post Reorganisation
Example: Rajya Sabha Representation
given: The Fourth Schedule allocates 4 Rajya Sabha seats to J&K.
steps: The 4 seats are filled by the Legislative Assembly of J&K.
Members are elected through proportional representation (single transferable vote).
The term of the members is 6 years.
The election is conducted by the Election Commission of India.
blocks.answer: The 4 seats are filled by the J&K Legislative Assembly through proportional representation.

blocks.title: Trap: Ladakh has Rajya Sabha seats.
blocks.correct: Ladakh has no Rajya Sabha seats. It is represented through nominated members.
blocks.tip: Ladakh has no legislature and no Rajya Sabha seats.

blocks.title: Key Points – Fourth Schedule
points: 4 Rajya Sabha seats to UT of J&K.
Elected by the J&K Legislative Assembly (proportional representation).
Ladakh has no Rajya Sabha seats.
Erstwhile state had 6 seats, now reduced to 4.

subtopics.title: Fifth Schedule – Application of Central Laws and Repeal of State Laws

blocks.title: Fifth Schedule – Legal Consolidation
blocks.subtitle: 106 Central Laws Applied, 153 State Laws Repealed

blocks.title: What is the Fifth Schedule?
blocks.content:
The Fifth Schedule of the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 is the legal mechanism for unifying the legal framework of the new UTs with the rest of India. It provides for:
1. **Application of 106 Central Laws** to J&K and Ladakh (e.g., IPC, CrPC, Indian Evidence Act, etc.).
2. **Repeal of 153 State Laws** that were previously applicable to the erstwhile state.

blocks.title: Key Central Laws Applied
blocks.content:
The following key Central Laws were applied to the UTs:
1. **Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860** – Criminal law.
2. **Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973** – Procedure for criminal trials.
3. **Indian Evidence Act, 1872** – Rules of evidence.
4. **Transfer of Property Act, 1882** – Property law.
5. **Indian Contract Act, 1872** – Contract law.
6. **Companies Act, 2013** – Corporate governance.
7. **Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017** – GST (already applied earlier).
8. **Right to Information Act, 2005** – Transparency.

blocks.title: Key State Laws Repealed
blocks.content:
The Act repealed 153 State Laws that were previously applicable to the erstwhile state of J&K. Some key repeals include:
1. **J&K Constitution Act, 1956** – The separate state constitution.
2. **J&K Ranbir Penal Code (RPC)** – Replaced by IPC.
3. **J&K Criminal Procedure Code** – Replaced by CrPC.
4. **J&K Land Revenue Act** – Replaced by central land laws.
5. **J&K Forest Act** – Replaced by central forest laws.
6. **J&K State Subject Laws** – Replaced by domicile laws.

blocks.title: Key Central Laws Applied vs State Laws Repealed
Example: Legal Unification
given: The Fifth Schedule unified the legal framework of J&K with the rest of India.
blocks.find: What was the significance of this unification?
steps: 106 Central Laws were applied, replacing the state-specific laws.
153 State Laws were repealed, including the J&K Constitution.
This brought J&K on par with other Indian states and UTs.
It simplified the legal system and ensured uniform application of laws.
It integrated J&K fully into the Indian legal framework.
blocks.answer: The Fifth Schedule integrated J&K into the Indian legal framework by applying Central Laws and repealing State Laws.

blocks.title: Trap: The J&K Constitution was retained.
blocks.wrong: The J&K Constitution Act, 1956 was retained after 2019.
blocks.correct: The J&K Constitution Act, 1956 was repealed under the Fifth Schedule.
blocks.tip: J&K Constitution was repealed; the Indian Constitution fully applies.

blocks.title: Key Points – Fifth Schedule
points: Legal unification with the rest of India.

subtopics.title: Delimitation Commission – Composition, Section 60, and SC/ST Reservations

blocks.title: What is the Delimitation Commission?
blocks.content: The Delimitation Commission is a constitutional body established to redraw the boundaries of assembly and parliamentary constituencies. For J&K, the Delimitation Commission was constituted under Section 60 of the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019. It was set up in 2020 to redraw the 83 existing assembly seats and to increase them to 90 (excluding the 24 reserved for PoK).

blocks.title: Section 60 – Delimitation of Constituencies
blocks.content:
Section 60 of the Act provides for the delimitation of assembly constituencies in the UT of J&K. Key provisions:
1. **Increase in Seats**: The number of seats increased from 83 to 90.
2. **Boundaries**: The Commission redraws constituency boundaries based on the latest census data.
3. **Reservation**: Seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes based on their population ratio.
4. **Delimitation Order**: The final order is published in the official gazette and is binding.

blocks.title: Composition of the Delimitation Commission
blocks.content:
The Delimitation Commission for J&K was chaired by a retired Supreme Court judge. Its members included:
1. **Chairperson**: A retired Supreme Court judge or a judge of a High Court.
2. **Chief Election Commissioner**: Ex-officio member.
3. **State Election Commissioner**: Ex-officio member.
4. **Representatives**: Officials from the Union Territory of J&K.

blocks.title: SC/ST Reservations
blocks.content: The Delimitation Commission reserved seats for Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) in proportion to their population. The reservation ensures adequate representation of these communities in the Legislative Assembly. The reservation is based on the latest census data.

blocks.title: Example: Delimitation Commission's Role
given: The Delimitation Commission increased J&K's assembly seats from 83 to 90.
blocks.find: What was the significance of this increase?
steps: The increase provided better representation to the people of J&K.
It adjusted the boundaries based on demographic changes.
It ensured SC/ST reservations based on population.
It excluded the 24 seats reserved for PoK, pending restoration.
The final order is binding and implemented in subsequent elections.
blocks.answer: The Delimitation Commission increased seats to ensure better representation and fairness.

blocks.title: Trap: The 24 PoK seats are included in the delimitation.
blocks.wrong: The 24 seats reserved for PoK are included in the current delimitation.
blocks.correct: The 24 seats reserved for PoK are not included in the current delimitation.
blocks.tip: PoK seats are reserved but not currently delimited.

blocks.title: Key Points – Delimitation Commission
points: Chaired by a retired Supreme Court judge.
Final order published in Gazette and binding.
